'''Central Wyoming Regional Airport''', formerly Riverton Regional Airport, {{airport codes|RIW|KRIW|RIW}} is three miles northwest of [[Riverton, Wyoming|Riverton]], in [[Fremont County, Wyoming|Fremont County]], [[Wyoming]];<ref name="FAA" /> it also serves nearby [[Lander, Wyoming]]. It is used for [[general aviation]] and sees one passenger airline. Service was subsidized by the [[Essential Air Service]] program until October 2006, when [[Great Lakes Airlines]] began providing subsidy-free service.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.regulations.gov/#!documentDetail;D=DOT-OST-2003-14536-0043 | title = Order 2006-9-9 | publisher = [[U.S. Department of Transportation]] | date = September 11, 2006}}</ref>  [[Key Lime Air]] operating as the [[Denver Air Connection]] began serving the airport with regional jet aircraft on July 1, 2016.

[[Federal Aviation Administration]] records say the airport had 17,035 passenger boarding's (enplanements) in [[calendar year]] 2008,<ref>
 {{cite web
 | url = http://www.faa.gov/airports/planning_capacity/passenger_allcargo_stats/passenger/media/cy08_all_enplanements.pdf
 | title = Enplanements for CY 2008 | format = PDF, 1.0 MB
 | work = CY 2008 Passenger Boarding and All-Cargo Data
 | publisher = Federal Aviation Administration | date = December 18, 2009
 }}
</ref> 14,186 in 2009 and 14,361 in 2010.<ref>
 {{cite web
 | url = http://www.faa.gov/airports/planning_capacity/passenger_allcargo_stats/passenger/media/cy10_all_enplanements.pdf
 | title = Enplanements for CY 2010 | format = PDF, 189 KB
 | work = CY 2010 Passenger Boarding and All-Cargo Data
 | publisher = Federal Aviation Administration | date = October 4, 2011
 }}
</ref> The [[National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems]] for 2011–2015 [[FAA airport categories|categorized]] it as a ''primary commercial service'' airport (more than 10,000 enplanements per year).<ref>
 {{cite web
 | url = http://www.faa.gov/airports/planning_capacity/npias/reports/media/2011/npias_2011_appA.pdf
 | title = 2011–2015 NPIAS Report, Appendix A | format = PDF, 2.03 MB
 | work = National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems
 | publisher = Federal Aviation Administration | date = October 4, 2010
 }}
</ref>

==Facilities==
The airport covers 1,250 [[acre]]s (506 [[hectare|ha]]) at an elevation of 5,528 feet (1,685 m). It has two [[Asphalt concrete|asphalt]] runways: 10/28 is 8,204 by 150 feet (2,501 x 46 m) and 1/19 is 4,800 by 75 feet (1,463 x 23 m).<ref name="FAA" /> The airport is an [[non-towered airport|uncontrolled airport]] with no control tower.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.airnav.com/airport/KRIW|title=AirNav: KRIW - Central Wyoming Regional Airport|website=www.airnav.com}}</ref>

In 2018 the airport had 4,547 aircraft operations, average 12 per day: 78% [[general aviation]], 22% [[air taxi]], and <1% military. 37 aircraft were then based at this airport: 86% single-engine, 11% multi-engine, and 3% helicopter.<ref name="FAA" />

==History==

===Historic airline service===
The original [[Frontier Airlines (1950-1986)]] served the airport for many years.  In 1950 Frontier [[Douglas DC-3]]s flew to Denver, Salt Lake City, Billings, Casper, Cheyenne and other cities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nov. 1, 1950 Frontier timetable |url=http://www.timetableimages.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.timetableimages.com}}</ref>  By 1964 Frontier had introduced [[Convair 580]]s nonstop to Denver, Casper, Jackson, WY, and Rock Springs and direct to Salt Lake City, Albuquerque, Billings, Cheyenne, Laramie and Cody.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aug. 1, 1964 Frontier timetable |url=http://www.timetableimages.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.timetableimages.com}}</ref>  Frontier Airlines predecessor [[Challenger Airlines]] served Riverton in the 1940s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Challenger Airlines timetable covers |url=http://www.timetableimages.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.timetableimages.com}}</ref>

In 1979 Frontier [[Boeing 737-200]]s began serving the airport, along with Convair 580s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nov. 15, 1979 Official Airline Guide |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref> Frontier 737s flew direct to Denver via Casper;<ref>{{Cite web |title=Feb. 1, 1980 & June 1, 1983 & June 1, 1984 Frontier Airlines route maps |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref> by 1985 Frontier had left the airport.<ref>{{Cite web |title=April 4, 1985 Frontier Airlines route map |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref>  Frontier was the only airline that flew mainline jets to the airport.

Frontier's service was replaced by Pioneer Airlines [[Swearingen Metroliner]]s nonstop to Denver, [[code sharing]] flights as [[Continental Express]] for [[Continental Airlines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Feb. 15, 1985 Official Airline Guide |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref> By 1989 [[Continental Express]] nonstops to Denver were [[Rocky Mountain Airways]] [[ATR 42]]s and [[Beechcraft 1900C]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dec. 15, 1989 Official Airline Guide |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref>  In 1995 the Continental Express code share service at the airport was being operated by [[GP Express Airlines]] with Beechcraft 1900Cs nonstop to Denver.<ref>{{Cite web |title=April 2, 1995 Official Airline Guide |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref> By 1991 [[United Express]] ([[Mesa Airlines]]) had joined Continental Express at the airport with [[Beechcraft 1900C]]s nonstop to Denver flown via a code sharing agreement with [[United Airlines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oct. 1, 1991 Official Airline Guide |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref>  Continental shut down its hub in Denver and by 1999 only [[United Express]] ([[Great Lakes Airlines]]) served the airport, with nonstop [[Beechcraft 1900]]s to Denver.<ref>{{Cite web |title=June 1, 1999 Official Airline Guide |url=http://www.departedflights.com/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.departedflights.com}}</ref>  Great Lakes later lost its United Express designation but continued to serve the airport as an independent airline before dropping Riverton.

===Recent developments===
[[Great Lakes Airlines]] previously served the airport with [[Beechcraft 1900D]]s. On November 1, 2016 Great Lakes introduced larger [[Embraer EMB-120 Brasilia]]s on most of its flights to Denver.<ref>http://www.greatlakesav.com {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191028060511/http://www.greatlakesav.com/ |date=2019-10-28 }}, Flight Info, Time Table</ref> However, Great Lakes soon went out of business, ending service to Riverton.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.flygreatlakes.com/ |title=Great Lakes Airlines |access-date=2021-06-28 |archive-date=2006-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060417140731/http://www.flygreatlakes.com/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[SkyWest Airlines]] operating as United Express replaced Key Lime Air service to Denver on January 12, 2020 when they took over the subsidized air service contract for Riverton and Sheridan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gillettenewsrecord.com/news/wyoming/article_375b0655-96e8-5d1c-b61f-e03e1311b439.html|title=SkyWest service to Riverton to begin in January|last=Exchange|first=Wyoming News|website=Gillette News Record|date=14 August 2019 |language=en|access-date=2019-08-24}}</ref>

In 2020, the name changed from '''Riverton Regional Airport''' to '''Central Wyoming Regional Airport'''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.airnav.com/airport/kriw|accessdate=2020-10-27|date=2020-10-08|website=AirNav.com|title=AirNav: KRIW - Central Wyoming Regional Airport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title="Central Wyoming Regional" is new name of Riverton's Airport|date=2020-08-21|accessdate=2020-10-27|url=https://wrrnetwork.com/2020/08/21/central-wyoming-regional-is-new-name-of-rivertons-airport/|website=WYO Today.com|publisher=Wind River Radio Network|archive-date=2020-10-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031030532/https://wrrnetwork.com/2020/08/21/central-wyoming-regional-is-new-name-of-rivertons-airport/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

It is used for general aviation and sees one passenger airline. Service was subsidized by the Essential Air Service program until October 2006, when Great Lakes Airlines began providing subsidy-free service.  Key Lime Air operating as the Denver Air Connection began serving the airport with regional jet aircraft on July 1, 2016.
Federal Aviation Administration records say the airport had 17,035 passenger boarding's (enplanements) in calendar year 2008, 14,186 in 2009 and 14,361 in 2010. The National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems for 2011–2015 categorized it as a primary commercial service airport (more than 10,000 enplanements per year).
